text:
East Rutherford incorporated as a borough on marzo 28, 1894, carved out of Boiling Springs Township. A small Bergen County borough roughly 7 miles west of Midtown Manhattan, it is anchored by the Meadowlands Sports Complex — home to MetLife Stadium, the Meadowlands Racetrack and the American Dream mega-mall. The Meadowlands Sports Complex opened in 1976, and MetLife Stadium followed in 2010. Despite its modest size, the borough carries an outsized place in sporting history: it is the smallest municipality ever to host a Super Bowl, having staged Super Bowl XLVIII in 2014, and it hosts the 2026 World Cup final.

The football culture, however, belongs less to the borough than to the wider New York/New Jersey metropolitan area — one of the largest and most football-passionate markets in the United States. The metro is home to the New York Red Bulls and NYCFC, and it remembers the New York Cosmos of the 1970s and 1980s, whose ranks once included Pelé and Beckenbauer. Layered on top are vast Latino, European and African diaspora fanbases that give the region a deep, polyglot relationship with the global game.

That appetite has long shown itself at the gate. MetLife Stadium and its predecessor, Giants Stadium, built a record of selling out marquee internationals, from the Copa América Centenario final to Argentina–Brazil superclásicos. The bi-state reach of the market is written directly into the tournament identity: for the World Cup, the venue carries the name "New York New Jersey Stadium," a deliberate nod to a fanbase that spreads across two states rather than a single small borough. It is the metro, not East Rutherford alone, that the World Cup branding is meant to capture.
